abstract: Maintains avalanche mitigation records and historical snowpack accumulation measurements
system_message:
You are the Avalanche and alpine hazard coordinator (AVAL), responsible for maintaining avalanche mitigation records and historical snowpack accumulation measurements across candidate research station sites, as well as tracking high-altitude meteorological data.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Alpine meteorological tracking（MET）
information_points.content:
AVAL-MET-E7X：According to weather station logs over the preceding three calendar years at Diavolezza Glacier Plateau, annual sub-zero windstorm days average 60 days.
AVAL-MET-67L：According to weather station logs over the preceding three calendar years at Gornergrat Ridge Observatory, annual sub-zero windstorm days average 75 days.
AVAL-MET-FB2：According to weather station logs over the preceding three calendar years at Jungfraujoch North Platform, annual sub-zero windstorm days average 45 days.

information_points.title: Maintains avalanche mitigation records and historical snowpack accumulation measurements（HAZ）
information_points.content:
AVAL-HAZ-F4J：For Jungfraujoch North Platform, an active avalanche defense system is installed along the station upslope perimeter barrier network featuring operational steel snow nets and gas-release stabilization fixtures, and the maximum annual snowpack accumulation measured over the past five winter seasons is 590 cm.
AVAL-HAZ-RRT：For Diavolezza Glacier Plateau, an active avalanche defense system is installed across the station upslope perimeter barrier network with operational steel snow nets and gas-release stabilization fixtures, and the maximum annual snowpack accumulation recorded over the past five winter seasons is 450 cm.
AVAL-HAZ-NIQ：For Gornergrat Ridge Observatory, an active avalanche defense system is installed along the station upslope perimeter barrier network with operational steel snow nets and gas-release stabilization fixtures, and the maximum annual snowpack accumulation recorded on level terrain over the past five winter seasons is 340 cm.
